text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said it was time to act against corrupt politicians and administrators, and that the Anti-Corruption Agency would be strengthened to deal with allegations of corruption and abuse of power.
-- The Malaysian team which conquered Mount Everest was given a rousing welcome at the Kuala Lumpur airport.

-- The high-end condominium market in southern Johor Baru city, across a short causeway from Singapore, is taking a breather as prices and rentals fell due to a supply glut, said Ricardo Wong of property consultants Colliers, Jordan Lee and Jaafar.

-- The Finance Ministry has approved the setting up of two wholly-owned Tenaga Nasional subsidiaries -- Tenaga Nasional Generation Sdn Bhd and TNB Engineers Sdn Bhd -- under a new group structure to take shape on September 1, said company executive chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali.

-- The Health Ministry has sought the help of the U.S. Centre for Disease Control to identify the baffling outbreak of a disease which has killed 14 young children in eastern Sarawak state, said health minister Chua Jui Meng.
-- The Shangri-La hotels chain, owned by Malaysian tycoon Robert Kuok, will invest $684 million to develop 16 more hotels by 2000, group communications director Joanne Watkins said in Hong Kong.
